blocks.heading: Cooperation and joint responsibility
blocks.text: Cooperation means people working together towards a shared objective. Joint responsibility means accepting a shared obligation for an outcome while retaining clear individual duties. Cooperation can reduce incompatible decisions, share knowledge and help departments solve problems together. It does not change the legal ownership of the enterprise. Shared responsibility also does not mean nobody is accountable: define contributions, authority and reporting so that an omission is not passed between departments. Different interests remain, and cooperation requires communication and fair treatment rather than an instruction to agree with management about everything.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: At Teya Furniture, sales staff consult production before promising delivery dates and both teams review whether customers receive complete orders. Shared information helps avoid impossible promises and supports reliable delivery. Sales remains responsible for accurate commitments and production for its schedule; joint responsibility links their efforts instead of removing those duties.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why workers sharing responsibility for a workshop’s delivery does not make the workshop a partnership.

Cooperation and joint responsibility describe how people coordinate work and accept obligations for an outcome. Partnership is an ownership form. Employees can cooperate in a company, sole trader or public enterprise without acquiring ownership.
